findings.title: Async legacy writes use the request context, so they are canceled as soon as the request completes
findings.body: In Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection, the goroutine that writes to LegacyStorage derives its context from the incoming request context (`ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`). The handler returns immediately after the unified-storage write, and the apiserver cancels the request context when the request finishes. Because the legacy write runs asynchronously, it will frequently observe an already-canceled parent context and fail with 'context canceled' (or the 10s timeout never even matters). The result is that the legacy store is silently not written for many (potentially most) operations, which defeats the stated purpose of mode 3 ('write to legacy as a safe measure') and leaves the two stores divergent. The goroutines should use a detached context, e.g. `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (plus the timeout), or a background context carrying only the logger.

findings.title: Create records storage failures under the legacy metric
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Create, when `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. This records a legacy-storage duration/latency observation for a failure that happened in the unified storage, corrupting the dual-writer metrics: legacy dashboards will show errors and latencies that never touched legacy storage, and no storage-side failure is recorded for the failing call. It should be `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`, as done in Delete/DeleteCollection.

findings.title: Update records storage failures under the legacy metric
findings.body: In DualWriterMode3.Update, the error path after `d.Storage.Update` fails calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)`. Same defect as in Create: a unified-storage failure is attributed to the legacy store in the metrics (wrong metric name, wrong latency sample, wrong error count). It should be `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.

findings.title: DeleteCollection records the async legacy write under the storage metric
findings.body: In the DeleteCollection goroutine, the result of `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)`. The legacy write outcome is attributed to the unified-storage metric instead of `recordLegacyDuration`, so legacy delete-collection failures/errors never show up in legacy metrics and pollute storage metrics. Compare with Delete (line 113) and Update (line 140), which correctly use recordLegacyDuration.

findings.title: Delete passes the object name as the 'kind' label on the success path
findings.body: On the successful-delete path, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes `name` (the deleted object's name) where every other call in this file passes `options.Kind` as the kind label. This creates unbounded metric label cardinality (one label value per deleted object name) and makes the delete metric rows inconsistent with all other methods. It should be `options.Kind`.

findings.title: Delete puts the base logger into the context instead of the enriched one
findings.body: In Delete, `log` is built with name/kind/method values, but the context is set with `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of `log`. Unlike every other method in this file, the request-scoped and derived contexts (including the async legacy-delete goroutine) lose the name/kind/method log fields, so any logs emitted downstream from the legacy delete carry no identifying information.

findings.title: Failures of the asynchronous legacy writes are never logged
findings.body: The previous implementation logged an error when the legacy write failed ('unable to create object in legacy storage', etc.). The new goroutines only record a Prometheus metric (`recordLegacyDuration(errObjectSt != nil, ...)`) and discard the error entirely; nothing is ever written to the log. Operators investigating a divergence between unified and legacy storage will have no log evidence of when or why the legacy write failed (timeout, conflict, validation error). The goroutines should at minimum log the returned error, e.g. `if err != nil { log.Error(err, "legacy write failed") }` (using a detached context for the logger).

findings.title: Async legacy Create mutates the request object concurrently with response serialization
findings.body: In Create, the goroutine passes the caller's `obj` (the same runtime.Object that `d.Storage.Create` was called with and whose result the handler serializes to the client) to `d.Legacy.Create`. Storage Create implementations commonly mutate the passed object in place (setting UID, resourceVersion, creation timestamp, generation). While the apiserver is serializing the response from the unified write, the legacy write goroutine can be mutating the same object concurrently — a data race that can produce corrupted response bodies or runtime panics under `-race`. The object passed to the legacy goroutine should be a deep copy, and the same consideration applies to `objInfo` in Update (the legacy Update runs objInfo.UpdatedObject against shared state while the handler may still be using it).

findings.title: Create error test never mocks Storage.Create, so the test exercises a mock panic instead of the error path
findings.body: The test case 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' (input failingObj) only sets up a legacy `Create` expectation via setupLegacyFn and leaves setupStorageFn nil. Mode3's Create calls `d.Storage.Create` first; the storageMock has no expectation for it, so the mock will panic ('mock: I don't know what to return because the method call was unexpected') rather than return an error. The test therefore does not verify the intended error path (and looks like the legacy/storage mock setups were swapped relative to the other tests, e.g. TestMode3_Delete which mocks storage only).

findings.title: Tests never assert that the asynchronous legacy write actually happens, and the shared mock is used from untracked goroutines
findings.body: Mode 3's defining behavior is that writes go to unified storage synchronously and to legacy storage asynchronously. None of the new tests assert that Legacy.Create/Delete/Update/DeleteCollection were invoked (e.g. via m.AssertExpectations or eventually-style waiting), so a regression that drops the legacy write entirely would still pass. Additionally, the legacy calls happen in fire-and-forget goroutines sharing the same non-thread-safe testify `mock.Mock` with the test goroutine, and the test returns without waiting for them — this is both a potential data race under -race and a source of flaky panics when the goroutine calls the mock after the test has finished. The tests should wait for the async write (e.g. a channel/signaled mock or polling on mock call counts) and then assert the legacy call happened.

findings.title: TestMode3_Get shadows the shared prometheus registry with a local one
findings.body: TestMode3_Get declares `p := prometheus.NewRegistry()` locally, shadowing the package-level `p` used by all other tests in the file (the PR even removed exactly this pattern from dualwriter_mode1_test.go). This is inconsistent and means the metrics registered for this test are silently different from every other mode-3 test; if the intent was to share one registry, this test diverges from it and a future reader can't tell whether it is intentional.
